pairs.why: Both are near twins, but A's thicker, chunkier slab and bigger checker squares sit slightly closer to the real table's heavy stone mass.
A's table is closer and chunkier, with larger squares and a softer stone finish, which matches the real card's bulky, simplified build a little better than B's thinner, more veined version.
The two docks are almost identical in rendering, colour and framing, and both differ from the real close-up in the same way, so neither is closer.
B is a close, chunky dock with warm orange wood and a large ring that fills the frame like the real card, while A is a tiny distant dock lost in the water.
B's thick posts, chunky red-and-white ring and softer matte wood read more like the real object's heavy, toy-solid build than A's thinner, glossier side view.
B frames thick posts, a coiled rope and a chunky ring up close like the real card, whereas A shows a small, far-off pier.
A's front-on, chunky posts and fat ring, in calmer matte colour, match the real card's solid mass better than B's glossier, thinner side view.
